issue_context.title: Remove/disable manual response chunking
issue_context.body:
If the application specifies a `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` response header then kestrel takes that as a signal that the app has implemented its own chunking and so the server should not auto-chunk. It's not clear that this feature has ever been used as intended, but it does keep breaking apps that are forwarding responses from HttpClient.

Example:
https://github.com/microsoft/reverse-proxy/blob/b2482f606a7dbcbc9b9797b04aed51138da0bd8d/src/ReverseProxy/Service/Proxy/HttpProxy.cs#L589-L594

Proposal: Disable and or remove this feature. Consider adding an option or quirk to re-enable it just in case anybody was using it.
comments: After giving this more thought, I think removing it is the right decision.

Thanks for contacting us.
We're moving this issue to the `Next sprint planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We will evaluate the request when we are planning the work for the next milestone. To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/master/docs/TriageProcess.md).

I'm all in favor of removing this behavior without a way to configure it via KestrelServerOptions. This behavior has been in Kestrel since pre-1.0, so it's still probably worth adding an AppContext switch just in case.

review_comments:
Can we pick a different name for this? This incorrectly implies Kestrel won't do auto-chunking when the switch is set.

"Switch.Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.DisableManualChunking" would be a better name, since what this is really doing is taking away the ability to manually write the chunk framing when you effectively opt out of Kestrel's auto chunking by setting the Transfer-Encoding header.
The polarity of DisableManualChunking is backwards, the default for a switch needs to be false.
Looks like this test fails here because the chunked header does reach the client. We should remove the header. I think it's a change in the same method you already fixed for http/1
We should also log something at the debug level to indicate we're ignoring the set "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" response header.

Even though it's probably correct to strip connection-specific header fields for HTTP/3 responses, citing the HTTP/2 spec doesn't confirm that.

It's also weird to cite all the other header fields that should be stripped like "Keep-Alive, Proxy-Connection, Transfer-Encoding, and Upgrade" and the "Connection" header itself and then only strip "Transfer-Encoding". We should either strip all of these now or save it for another PR. I'm leaning towards another PR.

The quote from the HTTP/3 spec is almost word for word the same.
https://quicwg.org/base-drafts/draft-ietf-quic-http.html#section-4.1.1

Yeah, I wanted to keep this PR focused on Transfer-Encoding issues.
